# Reference

What `vector` declares, generated from its source: the commands and their flags, the JSON files it reads and writes, and the modules it is built from. The guide shows them at work; this lists them all.

<scalar-grid cols="3">

<scalar-card title="Command line" icon="phosphor/regular/terminal-window">

[Every command](command-line.md) `vector` declares, its flags and arguments, and the 3 exit codes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="File formats" icon="phosphor/regular/brackets-curly" href="#file-formats">

The 3 JSON Schemas in `schemas/`.

</scalar-card>

The 121 source files of `src/`, from their doc comments.

</scalar-card>

## File formats

| Schema | What it describes |
| --- | --- |
| [`program.json`](formats/program.md) |  |
| [`rfc-contract.json`](formats/rfc-contract.md) | What a specification (an RFC, or markdown with numbered headings) requires of a set of functions: verbatim requirements, the functions' signatures, and the clauses (test vectors and properties) that check them. |
| [`spec-plan.json`](formats/spec-plan.md) |  |

## Modules

| Module | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| [`cli/diff`](modules/cli/diff.md) | `vector diff`: prove two programs equivalent, or show where they differ. |
| [`cli/spec-check`](modules/cli/spec-check.md) | `vector spec check`: check a contract's quotes and vectors against its source. |
| [`cli/spec-emit`](modules/cli/spec-emit.md) | `vector spec emit`: emit the test a contract implies. |
| [`cli/spec-exports`](modules/cli/spec-exports.md) | `vector spec exports`: refuse a new export its contract does not cover. |
| [`cli/spec-extract`](modules/cli/spec-extract.md) | `vector spec extract`: extract a contract from a kramdown-rfc spec's XML. |
| [`cli/spec-frozen`](modules/cli/spec-frozen.md) | `vector spec frozen`: refuse a change that edits a frozen contract. |
| [`cli/spec-mutate`](modules/cli/spec-mutate.md) | `vector spec mutate`: mutate the changed lines of the contract's module and refuse mutants the test misses. |
| [`cli/spec-run`](modules/cli/spec-run.md) | `vector spec run`: emit a contract's test and run it. |
| [`cli/spec-stale`](modules/cli/spec-stale.md) | `vector spec stale`: refuse a generated test that no longer matches its contract. |
| [`cli/verify`](modules/cli/verify.md) | `vector verify`: prove a program meets its spec plan. |
| [`core/diag`](modules/core/diag.md) | how vector reports a problem and which exit code it ends with. |
| [`core/fs`](modules/core/fs.md) | paths and directories: join, dirname, a recursive mkdir and fresh temporary directories. |
| [`core/hex`](modules/core/hex.md) | bytes as lowercase hex, random hex names, and SHA-256. |
| [`core/json`](modules/core/json.md) | reading and writing JSON through `nish/json-value`: parse a file into a document, read typed members with a clear error when one is missing or of the wrong kind, and write a document back with a final newline. |
| [`core/process`](modules/core/process.md) | running a child process with its input given and its output collected. |
| [`core/smt`](modules/core/smt.md) | reading what z3 prints: s-expressions, the numerals in a model, and a whole run's output split into one answer per query by the `(echo "@@Q<i>")` markers the script writes before each `(check-sat)`. |
| [`core/text`](modules/core/text.md) | ASCII case mapping that cannot panic. |
| [`core/z3`](modules/core/z3.md) | finding z3 and running one SMT-LIB2 script through it. |
| [`index`](modules/index.md) | the package's entry point, the module a Nish program reaches with `import { … } from "@amritk/vector"`. |
| [`lang/c`](modules/lang/c.md) | the C table: how C writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/cpp`](modules/lang/cpp.md) | the C++ table: how C++ writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/csharp`](modules/lang/csharp.md) | the C# table: how C# writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/dart`](modules/lang/dart.md) | the Dart table: how Dart writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/go`](modules/lang/go.md) | the Go table: how Go writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/java`](modules/lang/java.md) | the Java table: how Java writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/kotlin`](modules/lang/kotlin.md) | the Kotlin table: how Kotlin writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/names`](modules/lang/names.md) | how each language names a contract's functions, parameters and modules. |
| [`lang/php`](modules/lang/php.md) | the PHP table: how PHP writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/python`](modules/lang/python.md) | the Python table: how Python writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/ruby`](modules/lang/ruby.md) | the Ruby table: how Ruby writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/rust`](modules/lang/rust.md) | the Rust table: how Rust writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/swift`](modules/lang/swift.md) | the Swift table: how Swift writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/table`](modules/lang/table.md) | the shape of a language table: how each construct of the contract vocabulary (`spec/contract/vocab`) is written in one language, and what that language drops. |
| [`lang/tables`](modules/lang/tables.md) | the fourteen language tables, one for each language of `vocabLanguages`, in its order. |
| [`lang/typescript`](modules/lang/typescript.md) | the TypeScript table: how TypeScript writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`lang/zig`](modules/lang/zig.md) | the Zig table: how Zig writes each construct of the contract vocabulary, and what it drops. |
| [`main`](modules/main.md) | the binary's entry point. |
| [`spec/check`](modules/spec/check.md) | the pipeline every contract goes through: an ordered registry of gates, each a top-level function that reads the contract and returns its findings. |
| [`spec/contract/capacity`](modules/spec/contract/capacity.md) | The capacity of an out buffer: how many bytes a function that writes its result into `(out, at)` may write after `at`. |
| [`spec/contract/chars`](modules/spec/contract/chars.md) | the character-level checks a contract's text needs: UTF-8 decoding one code point at a time, control characters, and the patterns its ids, sections and numbers are written in. |
| [`spec/contract/contract`](modules/spec/contract/contract.md) | the entry to a contract: read its JSON, check its values, and hand back the model of `spec/contract/types`. |
| [`spec/contract/f64`](modules/spec/contract/f64.md) | a contract's f64 values: the text a literal is written in, and the binary64 encoding (IEEE 754-2019 §3.4) it reads as. |
| [`spec/contract/literals`](modules/spec/contract/literals.md) | the vector table's Call and Expected cells: `hexDecode("66")`, `"f"`, `[00 0f]`, `Key = 00ff`, `L = 42`, `22 x 0b`, `concat([00], [ff])`. |
| [`spec/contract/read`](modules/spec/contract/read.md) | a contract's JSON read into the model of `spec/contract/types`. |
| [`spec/contract/shape`](modules/spec/contract/shape.md) | the checks on a contract's values once its structure has been read: the patterns ids, sections, modules and literals are written in, the enums, the bounds of property variables, the source declarations and the references to them, and the free text copied into the generated test. |
| [`spec/contract/types`](modules/spec/contract/types.md) | the contract model, one class per object of `schemas/rfc-contract.json`. |
| [`spec/contract/typing`](modules/spec/contract/typing.md) | the types of a property clause's expressions. |
| [`spec/contract/vocab`](modules/spec/contract/vocab.md) | the neutral vocabulary a contract is written in: the value types of a signature, the literal kinds, the expression operators, the requirement levels and the languages a name can be overridden for. |
| [`spec/contract/write`](modules/spec/contract/write.md) | a contract written back as canonical JSON, the bytes `contracts/*.json` holds. |
| [`spec/emit/emit`](modules/spec/emit/emit.md) | a contract and its samples as a Nish test program. |
| [`spec/emit/file`](modules/spec/emit/file.md) | from a contract file to its test's text, and the test written to disk: what `vector spec emit` and `vector spec run` share. |
| [`spec/emit/go`](modules/spec/emit/go.md) | a contract and its samples as a Go test. |
| [`spec/emit/helpers`](modules/spec/emit/helpers.md) | the Nish helpers an emitted test may define. |
| [`spec/emit/lit`](modules/spec/emit/lit.md) | contract values as Nish source text: integers at their type, f64s, string literals, and the bytes a literal stands for. |
| [`spec/emit/packages`](modules/spec/emit/packages.md) | `--package <name>=<dir>`: where the modules of your own project live, so a test can import a module outside nish/. |
| [`spec/emit/python`](modules/spec/emit/python.md) | a contract and its samples as a Python test. |
| [`spec/emit/rust`](modules/spec/emit/rust.md) | a contract and its samples as a Rust test. |
| [`spec/emit/target`](modules/spec/emit/target.md) | what a test is emitted for: a language, the harness that runs it in that language, and whether its slow vectors run. |
| [`spec/emit/typescript`](modules/spec/emit/typescript.md) | a contract and its samples as a TypeScript test. |
| [`spec/extract`](modules/spec/extract.md) | `vector spec extract`: an RFC XML v3 spec (xml2rfc's output for a kramdown-rfc spec) to its canonical contract. |
| [`spec/front/front`](modules/spec/front/front.md) | the TypeScript front end. |
| [`spec/gates/cite`](modules/spec/gates/cite.md) | what the gates that read a contract's sources share: reading them once a run, finding the section a citation names, and naming a citation in a message ("RFC §2.2" in the main RFC, "rfc2104 §2" in another source). |
| [`spec/gates/completeness`](modules/spec/gates/completeness.md) | every binding sentence of the main source is accounted for. |
| [`spec/gates/coverage`](modules/spec/gates/coverage.md) | every binding requirement is checked by some clause, and every clause checks the module under test. |
| [`spec/gates/derive`](modules/spec/gates/derive.md) | the derived rule for a vector whose inputs are cited to one section of the main RFC and whose null, true or false result to another. |
| [`spec/gates/domain`](modules/spec/gates/domain.md) | every property's domain is inhabited, and its inputs are chosen. |
| [`spec/gates/fidelity`](modules/spec/gates/fidelity.md) | the contract says what its sources say. |
| [`spec/gates/ids`](modules/spec/gates/ids.md) | the ids gate: every requirement, function and clause id is unique, so a citation or a call names exactly one thing. |
| [`spec/gates/note`](modules/spec/gates/note.md) | how a gate records what it found. |
| [`spec/gates/provenance`](modules/spec/gates/provenance.md) | every vector's expected value comes from somewhere, and that holds. |
| [`spec/gates/result`](modules/spec/gates/result.md) | whether a section states a vector's result (null, true or false) rather than printing it. |
| [`spec/gates/run`](modules/spec/gates/run.md) | runs each vector's source command when `--run-sources` is given, and records what it printed for the provenance gate, which runs after it. |
| [`spec/gates/signatures`](modules/spec/gates/signatures.md) | the functions a contract declares for the module under test are what that module exports. |
| [`spec/gates/text`](modules/spec/gates/text.md) | how the fidelity and completeness gates read a section's text, without lookaround (nish/regex has none): word lists matched at word edges, the binding BCP 14 keywords, a labelled integer or f64, and the lines a value is printed on as a whole value. |
| [`spec/gates/typing`](modules/spec/gates/typing.md) | the typing gate: every vector calls a declared function with arguments and an expected value of its parameter and return types, and every property's `where` and `assert` are well-typed booleans over its variables (`where` may call nothing: a domain must be decidable without the implementation). |
| [`spec/gates/words`](modules/spec/gates/words.md) | the blocks of words a section prints, which a u16[], u32[] or u64[] vector value binds to. |
| [`spec/pr/cli`](modules/spec/pr/cli.md) | what the PR gates' commands share: reading `--format` and `--base`, and printing a report with the exit code it earns. |
| [`spec/pr/exports`](modules/spec/pr/exports.md) | every export a PR adds to or changes in a contract's target module is tested by the contract (one of its `functions`) or listed in its `outOfScope` with a reason, so no new surface lands untested. |
| [`spec/pr/frozen`](modules/spec/pr/frozen.md) | a PR changes the spec side (specs/, contracts/, rfcs/, and .refcache/, the kramdown-rfc reference cache a spec's build reads) or the implementation, never both, so a test cannot be loosened to match the code it tests; the one exception is a change that is only the rename of contracted exports on both sides (spec/pr/rename). |
| [`spec/pr/gitdiff`](modules/spec/pr/gitdiff.md) | what a change touches, read from git: the files it changes against a base and the lines of each it adds, and the exports a TypeScript module declares. |
| [`spec/pr/lex`](modules/spec/pr/lex.md) | a TypeScript module's tokens and top-level statements, as far as the export scanner needs them. |
| [`spec/pr/mutate`](modules/spec/pr/mutate.md) | the mutants of a module's changed lines, and the verdict on how the test met them. |
| [`spec/pr/mutaterun`](modules/spec/pr/mutaterun.md) | runs a test against each mutant of a module, several at once. |
| [`spec/pr/rename`](modules/spec/pr/rename.md) | the one change that may touch both sides of a frozen contract: renaming the functions it tests, and nothing else. |
| [`spec/pr/report`](modules/spec/pr/report.md) | what a PR gate found, and how it prints: as text, as markdown for a PR comment, or as JSON. |
| [`spec/pr/scope`](modules/spec/pr/scope.md) | the code a contract tests: the module's top-level declarations its functions reach. |
| [`spec/pr/stale`](modules/spec/pr/stale.md) | whether a generated test was emitted from the contract as it is now: its header comment's one `// vector-contract-sha256: <hex>` line must name the SHA-256 of the contract file's bytes. |
| [`spec/profile/profile`](modules/spec/profile/profile.md) | the vector profile: what an RFC XML v3 spec, built by kramdown-rfc and `xml2rfc --v2v3`, must say for vector to read a contract from it, and the reading. |
| [`spec/report/common`](modules/spec/report/common.md) | what every format of the check's report shares: the status, the findings placed where they are, the warnings shown, and how a citation, a requirement's evidence and a long text are written. |
| [`spec/report/json`](modules/spec/report/json.md) | the check's report as one JSON object, for tools: `{status, contract, issues, warnings, coverage, samples, sources, truncations, byteParts}`. |
| [`spec/report/markdown`](modules/spec/report/markdown.md) | the check's report as GitHub markdown, for a PR comment: each requirement's quote, then the clauses that cover it; then the source commands, the exclusions and the warnings. |
| [`spec/report/text`](modules/spec/report/text.md) | the check's report for a terminal: the status, every finding, each requirement with the clauses that cover it, the source commands, the exclusions and the warnings. |
| [`spec/run/command`](modules/spec/run/command.md) | `vector spec run`: emit a contract's test, run it (with a nish install, or the language's own interpreter), and report the verdict per requirement. |
| [`spec/run/run`](modules/spec/run/run.md) | running an emitted test against a nish install, and reading its transcript back in the contract's terms: which requirement each `PASS` / `FAIL` line speaks to, and whether the transcript is the one the test's own `main` wrote. |
| [`spec/sample/eval`](modules/spec/sample/eval.md) | evaluates a property's call-free expressions, its `where` above all, as the generated test does: + - * % wrap to their operands' integer type, `and` and `or` stop at the first deciding operand, and `unwrap(null)` is undefined, which makes `where` false. |
| [`spec/sample/ints`](modules/spec/sample/ints.md) | the integers a property's variables take, held in an i64 whatever their type. |
| [`spec/sample/prng`](modules/spec/sample/prng.md) | the seeded generator random samples are drawn from. |
| [`spec/sample/property`](modules/spec/sample/property.md) | chooses a property's inputs: the boundaries Z3 finds in its integer skeleton, then seeded random draws, every one kept only when its `where` evaluates to true. |
| [`spec/sample/smt`](modules/spec/sample/smt.md) | the integer skeleton of a property, which Z3 searches for boundary inputs. |
| [`spec/source/fold`](modules/spec/source/fold.md) | GENERATED; do not edit it by hand. |
| [`spec/source/hidden`](modules/spec/source/hidden.md) | text that reads one way to a reviewer and another to the gates. |
| [`spec/source/load`](modules/spec/source/load.md) | a contract's sources, found, confined, pinned and read. |
| [`spec/source/path`](modules/spec/source/path.md) | where a contract's source is read from, and the refusal of a file that is not spec text. |
| [`spec/source/rfc`](modules/spec/source/rfc.md) | an RFC's plain-text rendering (rfc-editor.org's rfcNNNN.txt), read well enough to answer two questions deterministically: 1. |
| [`spec/xml/doc`](modules/spec/xml/doc.md) | an RFC XML v3 document read into what extract needs: its sections numbered as xml2rfc numbers them, each read as lines, the sentences its `<bcp14>` markup makes normative, its references, and the text each `<xref>` prints when the preptool has not worked it out. |
| [`spec/xml/reader`](modules/spec/xml/reader.md) | a narrow XML reader for RFC XML v3 (RFC 7991), as xml2rfc and kramdown-rfc write it. |
| [`spec/xml/text`](modules/spec/xml/text.md) | RFC XML v3 as the plain text xml2rfc's text writer prints, and the blocks of a section read as lines. |
| [`verify/emit/dashboard`](modules/verify/emit/dashboard.md) | the proof report as a 70-column box: each function's Hoare triple, one mark per postcondition, the counterexamples and hazards the solver found, the float64 gate's findings, and a verdict. |
| [`verify/emit/float64`](modules/verify/emit/float64.md) | the float64 gate. |
| [`verify/emit/outjson`](modules/verify/emit/outjson.md) | a small JSON tree for vector's `--json` output, rendered the way `JSON.stringify(v, null, 2)` renders it: two-space indentation, keys in insertion order, `[]` and `{}` for empty containers. |
| [`verify/emit/typescript`](modules/verify/emit/typescript.md) | the TypeScript a proven program compiles to: a direct transliteration of the expressions the solver proved, with domain guards on every parameter and each requires clause as a runtime throw. |
| [`verify/equiv/diff`](modules/verify/equiv/diff.md) | the regeneration gate: prove that a new version of a program behaves exactly as the old one did, or show the inputs where it does not. |
| [`verify/lang/ast`](modules/verify/lang/ast.md) | vector-lang, the expression language a program is written in, as Nish classes: an expression tree, the clauses and functions built from it, and the spec plan whose axioms the clauses cite. |
| [`verify/lang/check`](modules/verify/lang/check.md) | the semantic checks no schema can express, run on a program whose shape `verify/lang/read` accepted: name resolution, monomorphic types, `result` only in ensures, layering (calls go strictly downward, so the call graph is a DAG and inlining terminates), agreement with the spec plan's units, and axiom traceability. |
| [`verify/lang/pretty`](modules/verify/lang/pretty.md) | renders vector-lang expressions for people: the `math` style for the dashboard and feedback (`∧`, `∨`, `⇒`, `¬`), and the `ts` style for emitted TypeScript (`&&`, `===`, `Math.abs`), with only the parentheses precedence needs. |
| [`verify/lang/read`](modules/verify/lang/read.md) | reads a program and a spec plan out of parsed JSON, checking their shape against `schemas/program.json` and `schemas/spec-plan.json`. |
| [`verify/lang/style`](modules/verify/lang/style.md) | advisory checks that never gate a proof. |
| [`verify/smt/script`](modules/verify/smt/script.md) | translates a typechecked vector-lang program into one SMT-LIB2 script for z3: per function, a reachability query, a proof and a triviality query per ensures clause, and a query per division, per callee precondition and per Int operation the emitted code evaluates. |
| [`verify/solve/replay`](modules/verify/solve/replay.md) | re-evaluates, without z3, each input z3 says breaks a program: a counterexample to an ensures clause, an input that reaches a hazard, a witness of `vector diff`. |
| [`verify/solve/report`](modules/verify/solve/report.md) | runs a program's verification script through z3 and reads the answers into a report. |
| [`verify/verify`](modules/verify/verify.md) | the whole deterministic gate over a spec plan and a program: shape, types, the plan's decomposition, axiom traceability, z3, then the float64 gate. |
